description: The numeric-code cascade at :322-337, arm one - the last construct inside VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS that no other case in this folder reaches. RISK R-B STATED FIRST, BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:222 '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |', which is the inverse of the prompt's mapping and the mirror image of parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. Rule R1 resolves it - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure, so the divergence is documented here and never silently corrected; the Agent Action Plan escalates it for explicit user confirmation, and nothing here guesses which artefact is authoritative about intent, only about behaviour, where the source is the only oracle there is. This case is not downgraded to a read-only expectation to match the name: it refuses an add, and it refuses it while CONFIRMI already holds 'Y', which is the strongest demonstration available that the refusal belongs to the guard and not to the confirmation. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: the first arm of the EVALUATE TRUE at :322-337, which is the numeric class test on the two code fields. :323 is WHEN TTYPCDI OF COTRN2AI NOT NUMERIC, and its action block is :324-328 - MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG, MOVE 'Type CD must be Numeric...' TO WS-MESSAGE, MOVE -1 TO TTYPCDL OF COTRN2AI, PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN. TTYPCDI is typed 'AB'. app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY declares TTYPCDI PIC X(2), so two characters fill the item exactly and no padding decision is involved; the COBOL class test on an alphanumeric item is true only when every character is a digit, so 'AB' fails it and the arm is taken. EVALUATE is ordered and first-match-wins, so TTYPCD is tested BEFORE TCATCD (rule R7, gate G30): TCATCDI is therefore typed '0001', four digits filling its PIC X(4) exactly, which passes the class test and leaves arm two unreachable in this run. Every other field carries the same valid value case15 uses, so this case and case15 differ in exactly one input - two characters - and the whole difference in outcome is attributable to that one field. THE FOUR SIBLING GUARDS OF THIS CHAIN, DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN RE-CASED (gate G15 - this folder holds exactly twenty case files, so the siblings are recorded here with their literals and their cursor targets instead of being given files of their own): (1) arm two of this same EVALUATE, :329-334, WHEN TCATCDI OF COTRN2AI NOT NUMERIC, reports 'Category CD must be Numeric...' and moves -1 into TCATCDL. (2) The originating-date format check, EVALUATE TRUE at :353-366, reports 'Orig Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' and moves -1 into TORIGDTL. (3) The processing-date format check, EVALUATE TRUE at :368-381, reports 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' and moves -1 into TPROCDTL. (4) The merchant-id check, :430-436, reports 'Merchant ID must be Numeric...' and moves -1 into MIDL. Two details of those four are easy to lose and are stated explicitly (practice B5, which requires every guard to survive as written): the two 'must be Numeric...' literals carry a trailing ellipsis of three dots and the two 'should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' literals carry NO trailing ellipsis at all, so a translation that regularised the punctuation would change what the terminal displays; and the merchant-id guard is a standalone IF, not an arm of any EVALUATE, positioned at :430 AFTER both CALL 'CSUTLDTC' sites at :393 and :413, which makes it the LAST guard in the paragraph rather than a member of the numeric cascade it superficially resembles. THE DATE DECOMPOSITION, WHICH IS WHY THOSE TWO CHECKS ARE POSITIONAL AND NOT SEMANTIC: each date EVALUATE collapses FIVE WHEN conditions onto ONE shared action block, so the first condition that holds rejects and the remaining ones are never evaluated. Over TORIGDTI they are (1:4) IS NOT NUMERIC for the four-digit year, (5:1) NOT EQUAL '-' for the first separator, (6:2) NOT NUMERIC for the two-digit month, (8:1) NOT EQUAL '-' for the second separator and (9:2) NOT NUMERIC for the two-digit day; the windows sum to 4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10, which is exactly the PIC X(10) the symbolic map declares, so the check reads every byte of the field and no byte twice (practice B11). :368-381 applies the identical five windows to TPROCDTI. THE FULL ORDER INSIDE VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS, WITH THE CASE THAT OWNS EACH STEP: the paragraph opens at :235 with IF ERR-FLG-ON blanking the eleven detail fields at :238-248, which PROCESS-ENTER-KEY cannot reach because a raised flag has already terminated the task, and which is preserved as written (practice B5); then the eleven-arm empty-field EVALUATE at :251-320, whose first arm is driven by case03 and whose WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :318 is what every later case relies on; then this numeric cascade at :322-337, driven here; then the positional amount check at :339-351, driven by case13; then the originating-date format check at :353-366, driven by case14; then the processing-date format check at :368-381, documented above; then the FUNCTION NUMVAL-C conversion and re-render at :383-386; then CALL 'CSUTLDTC' on the originating date at :393, whose accepting outcome is driven by case15 and whose rejecting outcome by case17; then CALL 'CSUTLDTC' on the processing date at :413, rejected by case18; then the merchant-id IF at :430-436, documented above; and the paragraph ends at :437. WHY EXACTLY ONE MESSAGE, AND WHY IT APPEARS ON TWO CHANNELS: SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN at :516-534 ends with EXEC CICS RETURN at :530-534, and in CICS RETURN terminates the task - control never comes back to the statement after the PERFORM. One guard firing therefore means the amount check, both date format checks, the NUMVAL-C re-render, both CSUTLDTC calls, the merchant-id check, the EVALUATE CONFIRMI at :169 and ADD-TRANSACTION are all unreached in this run, which is why TRNAMTI is reported back exactly as it was typed rather than re-rendered through the PIC +99999999.99 mask, why no date utility is invoked, and why nothing is written. Exactly ONE message text is produced - 'Type CD must be Numeric...' - and it is pinned twice because the program moves it through two receivers of different width: WS-MESSAGE is PIC X(80) in WORKING-STORAGE at :38, and :520 moves it into ERRMSGO, which app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY declares PIC X(78), so the move loses the last two bytes on the way to the screen. Both widths are written out in full, space-padded on the right as a MOVE to an alphanumeric receiver pads (rule R5), because a two-byte truncation that nobody pins is a two-byte truncation nobody has checked. The cursor is TTYPCDL and no other length item holds -1: a length item is validation metadata and never a payload member, which is why it is reported under its own name rather than under the field's. WHAT IS SEEDED, AND WHY IT IS SEEDED THAT WAY: CCXREF carries five rows of the cardxref fixture exactly as they ship, 36 bytes wide, and is deliberately NOT pre-padded - app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares CARD-XREF-RECORD as 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = 50 and the shipped data omits the trailing FILLER PIC X(14), so the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below supplies those fourteen spaces once, at seed time, and is the sole owner of that repair (gate G16, risk R-F). The key resolution reads that dataset through its alternate index: ACTIDINI is eleven digits so the arm at :196 is taken, FUNCTION NUMVAL at :204 converts it, :206-207 move the eleven-digit image into XREF-ACCT-ID and back over the screen field, READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :578 returns DFHRESP(NORMAL) - the arm at :587 - and :209 moves XREF-CARD-NUM into CARDNINI. The account 00000000050 and the card 0500024453765740 are the first row of the fixture read at its declared offsets, positions 26 to 36 for the account identifier and 1 to 16 for the card number, so both values are the shipped data rather than invented ones (gate G47). CXACAIX is NOT seeded as a dataset of its own: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:63-65 defines it as a PATH over the CCXREF base, so the alternate-index read resolves through the one seeded base cluster and never through a second table (gate G45). TRANSACT is declared inline with three 350-byte rows because no ASCII fixture ships for that master - it is populated online, not loaded - and no tenth fixture is named, the set being closed at the nine derived from app/data/ASCII. Every dataset is addressed by its application.yml binding key rather than by name, so not one fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears in this file (gate G46), and the code page is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION AND IS PRESERVED AS ONE (practice B5): WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' is declared at :40 and COPY CVACT01Y at :89, and neither is referenced anywhere in the program's 783 lines - no DATASET operand names WS-ACCTDAT-FILE and no field of ACCOUNT-RECORD is ever moved - so the account master is a dead declaration and its copybook a dead include. No ACCTDAT input is declared here and no ACCTDAT row appears in any expectation, in this case or in any other in this folder: ParityHarness.seed states that the inputs member names every dataset the unit under test will read, so seeding a master the program never opens would assert a read that does not exist. The deadness is asserted as the non-event it is, and COTRN02CParityTest.DeadDeclarations proves the translation keeps both names as constants and wires no account collaborator at all. TWO RECONCILIATIONS RECORDED IN THE OPEN RATHER THAN MADE SILENTLY (practice B4): first, this file's authoring brief listed ACCTDAT among the datasets to seed while simultaneously requiring that ACCTDAT be documented as dead. Only one of those can be true of a run, and the harness contract decides which: a seeded dataset is an assertion that the unit reads it, so ACCTDAT is omitted from inputs and its deadness is stated instead. Second, the same brief attributed the amount-mask check to case15 and the empty-field cascade to case08 and case12. In this folder as built those steps belong to case13 and case03, while case08 and case12 drive FUNCTION NUMVAL's rejection on the account and card key fields and case15 drives CSUTLDTC's accepting outcome. The order-of-execution map above therefore records the OWNERS THAT EXIST rather than repeating the brief's attribution, because that map is only useful if a reader can follow it to a real file, and because practice B12 admits nothing that has not been checked. BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS, SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, cross-checked against the symbolic-map widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY (twenty-one payload items whose lengths sum with their length, flag and attribute metadata and the leading twelve-byte filler to a 555-byte group image; ERRMSGO PIC X(78)), against the copybook byte layouts (app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy as 4 + 8 + 4 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 25 + 25 + 11 + 1 + 16 + 7 + 7 = 160 bytes and the CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension at :72-80 as 16 + 16 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 16 = 58, so the area travelling in the payload is 218 and the extension stays a field of its own rather than being folded into the 160; app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy 350; app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy 50), against the screen literals of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, and against the real bytes of app/data/ASCII. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, which Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers - among them a compiler whose indexed-file handler is disabled, the absence of any Language Environment CEE service behind CSUTLDTC, the absence of a CICS emulator, and the absence of the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA copybooks this program copies at :92-93 - and the change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. The attention identifier is DFHENTER, taken from common.CicsAid, which reproduces that absent DFHAID from IBM CICS documentation (risk R-D). NO USER RULES EXIST: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the whole document, so no user rule forces this file into scope and no user rule constrains how it is written. Their absence is stated explicitly and is not treated as permission to lower the bar: the standard held here is the Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 enterprise practices, cited by name where they bite - B1 (all five literals of this chain reproduced from the source rather than paraphrased, and no placeholder anywhere), B3 (the reference trees app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd and app/data are read-only and were not touched), B4 (the R-B inversion and both reconciliations disclosed), B5 (the dead declarations, the punctuation of each literal and the merchant-id guard's position all preserved), B7 (the clock pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the one instant all twenty cases in this folder use, and the two date inputs pinned to the fixed literal 2022-07-18 rather than computed from today, so the run is deterministic in any timezone and on any day), B8 (the chosen non-numeric code stated outright, every other field's value given explicitly, each message pinned at both its widths, binding keys instead of dataset names and a named code page), B11 (every width summed from a PICTURE clause) and B12 (the provenance and the reconciliations above). Rules R1, R5, R6 and R7 bind as well; there is no GO TO anywhere in this program's 783 lines, so R7 costs nothing here beyond keeping the EVALUATE arms in source order with WHEN OTHER last. GATES DISCHARGED: G15 (one of exactly twenty cases, with the four sibling guards documented instead of given files), G16 (the cardxref seed stays 36 bytes and is normalised once at seed time), G18 (the diff count must be zero, per module rather than per build), G30 (the ordered numeric EVALUATE is driven on its first arm, with arm two and WHEN OTHER both shown to be unreachable in this run by the values chosen), G37 (no server-side session state - the whole 218-byte area travels in the payload), G38 (the REENTER half of the pair: CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at '1' so :120 sends the run down the receive path, the error flag is raised and the cursor is requested with MOVE -1; this screen has no CSSETATY include, so no field is coloured and ERRMSGC stays the default), G45 (CXACAIX is an alternate-index finder over the CCXREF base, not a second table), G46 (binding keys, never a dataset-name literal), G47 (the DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm of READ-CXACAIX-FILE on the way in) and G51 (the controller is driven as a plain object - no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path). DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, because COTRN02C has none of them or because they belong elsewhere: G32 (zero GO TO, so no backward jump to restructure), G35 (zero CALL 'CEE3ABD', which is why the return code is 0 and no abend path exists), G39 (no pagination loop on this screen), G40 (no XCTL on this path - the task ends at EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CT02'), and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD binds CT02 back to COTRN02C, which is why the next program is this program), G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC in this program) and G12 (CSUTLDTC is never invoked on this path, so the claim that it is a service and not a job belongs to case15, case17 and case18).
